newsitem.title: UK: Spain euro deal is the focus of Eurobond activity.
newsitem.headline: Spain euro deal is the focus of Eurobond activity.

text.p: Spain's first Bono-exchangeable Eurobond, a well-received 1.5 billion euro ($1.65 billion) deal, was the highlight of new issue business on Thursday.
The 6.00 percent deal, due January 2008 and designed to be exchangeable into an outstanding Bono with the same coupon and maturity, was increased from an initial 1.25 billion euros.
"The increase speaks for itself...it was massively oversubscribed and we've seen it tighten by at least one basis point," said one trader closer to the deal.
Another dealer said the issue, reoffered at a 15 basis points spread, was testing 13.5 b.p.

There was talk of the deal having an 18-20 b.p. spread earlier in the week. The bond will be traded as an Ecu instrument until the advent of EMU. Prior to today's financing, Spain had no outstanding Ecu paper.

French and Spanish benchmark 10-year bonds, denominated in francs and pesetas respectively, were trading at a spread of 76 b.p. A franc deal for Spain launched earlier this year was trading at a 14-15 b.p. spread, dealers said.
The joint lead managers were Banco Central Hispano, Banco Santander de Negocios, Paribas and SBC Warburg.
SBC Warburg managing director Manfred Schepers said the bond had been bought by "a diverse group of institutional investors across Europe, showing the broad commitment to the euro".

The third stage of European economic and monetary union, including the introduction of the European Union's planned single currency, the euro, is prescribed by EU law to take place no later than January 1, 1999.
From that date, all national currencies within the euro area will cease to exist legally and will instead be expressions of the euro.
Elsewhere, United Export Import Bank (Uneximbank) became the latest Russian bank to launch a Eurobond, this time a $200 million three-year funding at a 400 b.p. spread via Merrill Lynch and ICFI.
Uneximbank in January made the first unsecured borrowing in the international capital markets for a Russian company by privately placing a $50 million three-year FRN.
Uneximbank was founded in 1993 by a number of Russian export and trading companies.
Abbey National and Hewlett-Packard both launched short-dated retail-targeted dollar Eurobonds.
Abbey National's was a $250 million two-year which was holding at its 14 b.p. reoffer level while Hewlett-Packard's $200 million three-year was steady at an eight b.p. spread.
